narrative.hero: Learning to sense the physical world
narrative.bio: I study how measurement physics can help learning systems perceive the physical world. My research connects optical measurement design with learned representations for image reconstruction and image-free perception. I am now exploring acquisition-aware learning and interfaces between optical signals and pretrained multimodal models. My long-term goal is to build sensing systems that learn what to measure next.
narrative.direction: During my current visit at Politecnico di Milano, I plan to extend this work to time-domain diffuse optics and three-dimensional reconstruction, investigating how physical modeling can support transfer from simulation to optical experiments.
narrative.welcome: I welcome research collaborations and research internship opportunities in computational imaging, physics-aware machine learning, and multimodal sensing.
narrative.resume_summary: I work on optical measurement design and learning for imaging and perception. Current research explores acquisition-aware learning and pretrained models for optical signals.
narrative.long_term: Longer term, I aim to develop perception that helps a system decide what to measure next and learn through interaction with the physical world.
narrative.internship_summary: PhD student working on computational imaging and learning from optical measurements. Research experience spans measurement design, image reconstruction, and image-free perception.
narrative.current_summary: Developing acquisition-aware models and adapting pretrained multimodal models to bucket-detector signals. Planned visiting research: time-domain diffuse optics and 3D reconstruction.

projects.title: The Lift Spectrum · Robust image-free perception
projects.summary: Our image-free segmentation is more robust to measurement noise than the tested reconstruct-then-segment baselines when models are trained on clean data.
bullets: Demonstrated greater robustness to measurement noise than the tested reconstruct-then-segment baselines, with all models trained on clean data.
Learned spatial task representations directly from single-pixel measurements, using reconstruction only as auxiliary supervision.

projects.title: Sparse Hadamard single-pixel imaging
projects.summary: Tunable-sparsity Hadamard illumination for noise-resilient single-pixel imaging, supported by theory and optical experiments.
bullets: Designed tunable-sparsity Hadamard illumination for noise-resilient single-pixel imaging; developed a noise model and validated the approach in optical experiments.

projects.title: LDGI · Optical phased-array imaging
projects.summary: A loop differential ghost-imaging algorithm for line-pattern illumination from one-dimensional optical phased arrays.
bullets: Developed loop differential ghost imaging for line patterns from one-dimensional optical phased arrays; validated the algorithm in simulations and optical experiments.

projects.title: Acquisition-aware learning and multimodal measurement interfaces
projects.summary: Developing models that account for measurement conditions, and adapting pretrained multimodal models to bucket-detector signals.
bullets: Developing acquisition-aware models for reconstruction and perception across changing measurement budgets and acquisition conditions.
Adapting pretrained multimodal models to detector signals, with current work on fine-tuning for direct interpretation of bucket measurements.

directions.title: Learning with acquisition physics
directions.description: I am developing models that incorporate how signals are acquired, and studying how learned representations behave when acquisition conditions change.

directions.title: Connecting optical signals and pretrained models
directions.description: I am adapting pretrained multimodal models to bucket-detector signals, exploring how prior visual knowledge can support inference directly from measurements.

directions.title: Time-domain diffuse optics and 3D reconstruction
directions.description: During my current visit at Politecnico di Milano, I plan to investigate light-transport modeling and learning-based inversion for three-dimensional reconstruction.

platform_copy.linkedin_about:
I study how measurement physics can help learning systems perceive the physical world. My research includes noise-resilient Hadamard measurement design, ghost-imaging algorithms for optical phased arrays, and image-free segmentation. In The Lift Spectrum, image-free segmentation better withstands measurement noise than the tested reconstruct-then-segment baselines after training on clean data.

I am currently exploring acquisition-aware learning and pretrained multimodal models for optical signals. My long-term goal is to develop sensing systems that learn what to measure next. I welcome research collaborations and internship opportunities in computational imaging, physics-aware machine learning, and multimodal sensing.
